findings.description: The 'data' bucket is created with no ACL restriction and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and the inline comment explicitly states the bucket is public. Anonymous users may be able to list and read objects, including the customer master spreadsheet uploaded to it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects containing customer data are stored without enforced server-side encryption, unlike the logs bucket which uses SSE-KMS.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorised access to this publicly reachable bucket holding customer data would leave no audit trail for detection or forensics.
There is no bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects in this internet-exposed bucket can be read or written over plaintext HTTP.

A file named 'customer-master.xlsx' — apparently a master list of customer records — is uploaded into the unencrypted, publicly accessible 'data' bucket with no per-object KMS encryption, exposing sensitive PII to anonymous readers.
The financials bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial records stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial data, so there is no audit trail of object access or tampering.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket; the private ACL is the only control, so a future ACL or bucket policy change could silently expose financial data publicly.
No bucket policy denies non-TLS requests, permitting financial data to transit in cleartext over HTTP.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operations data is stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured, leaving no record of who accessed or modified objects in this bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, so subsequent ACL or policy changes could expose it to the internet without a backstop control.
The data science bucket has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so datasets likely derived from customer and financial data are unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, removing the defence-in-depth control against future public ACLs or bucket policies.

The central log bucket, which aggregates access logs from other buckets and uses the 'log-delivery-write' ACL, has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so an accidental public-read grant would expose aggregated audit data.
No bucket policy denies non-TLS requests, so log data can be written or read over unencrypted HTTP.
